title: Microbench quant cost sampler
content:
Purpose:
Quick spreadsheet-style sampler to estimate token-level cost, throughput impact, and quality delta for candidate quantization strategies (FP8, INT8, 4-bit variants).

Context / constraints (working notes):
- We want a cheap way to triage whether model X is a good candidate for 4-bit or INT8/FP8 given: average prompt length, average generation length, batching profile, and quality budget (e.g., allowed eval metric drop).
- This is intentionally lightweight — uses per-batch latency microbench numbers and simple multiplicative cost models rather than full scheduler sims.

Key spreadsheet columns (name | units | description):
- config_name | text | e.g., fp8-default, int8-qat, 4bit-ptq
- model_size | tokens | rough model param class label (7B/13B/70B)
- gpu_hour_cost | $/hour | raw infrastructure cost for a reference GPU (e.g., a40/rtx6000/p4d).
- peak_tokens_per_sec | tps | measured tokens/sec at steady state for single-request microbench (no batching)
- batch_size | tokens | typical batch size used in production (sum of input+gen tokens)
- effective_tps_batch | tps | estimated tokens/sec under target batching (see formula below)
- kv_cache_factor | multiplier | 0-1 multiplier to account for prefix caching (0.3 if heavy caching)
- accuracy_delta_pct | pct | percent absolute drop in eval metric (e.g., LlamaEval accuracy) compared to FP16 baseline
- quality_budget_pct | pct | maximum allowed drop (input from product)
- cost_per_1k_tokens | $ | computed output (see formulas)
- recommendation | text | keep / consider / avoid (heuristic output)

Representative formula notes to paste into sheet cells (pseudo-formulas):
- effective_tps_batch = peak_tokens_per_sec * (batch_size / reference_batch) * batch_efficiency_factor * kv_cache_factor
  - reference_batch is the microbench batch used to measure peak_tokens_per_sec (documented in cell)
  - batch_efficiency_factor: empirical factor (0.6-1.2) describing how well the runtime scales with batch size
- token_cost_hour = gpu_hour_cost / (effective_tps_batch * 3600)
- cost_per_1k_tokens = token_cost_hour * 1000
- relative_cost_vs_fp16 = cost_per_1k_tokens / fp16_cost_per_1k_tokens

Quick example rows (toy numbers, for engineering triage):
- row A: config_name = fp16-baseline, model_size=13B, gpu_hour_cost=$3.00, peak_tokens_per_sec=600, batch_size=2048, reference_batch=512, batch_efficiency_factor=0.9, kv_cache_factor=1.0, accuracy_delta_pct=0.0, quality_budget_pct=2.0
  - effective_tps_batch = 600 * (2048/512) * 0.9 * 1.0 = 600 * 4 * 0.9 = 2160 tps
  - token_cost_hour = 3.00 / (2160 * 3600) = 3.00 / 7,776,000 ≈ 3.86e-7 $/token => cost_per_1k_tokens ≈ $0.000386
- row B: config_name = int8-ptq, model_size=13B, gpu_hour_cost=$2.40, peak_tokens_per_sec=820, batch_size=2048, reference_batch=512, batch_efficiency_factor=0.9, kv_cache_factor=1.0, accuracy_delta_pct=1.1, quality_budget_pct=2.0
  - effective_tps_batch = 820 * 4 * 0.9 = 2952 tps
  - token_cost_hour = 2.40 / (2952 * 3600) = 2.40 / 10,627,200 ≈ 2.26e-7 $/token => cost_per_1k_tokens ≈ $0.000226
- row C: config_name = 4bit-ptq, model_size=13B, gpu_hour_cost=$1.95, peak_tokens_per_sec=1200, batch_size=2048, reference_batch=512, batch_efficiency_factor=1.0, kv_cache_factor=0.95, accuracy_delta_pct=2.6, quality_budget_pct=2.0
  - effective_tps_batch = 1200 * 4 * 1.0 * 0.95 = 4560 tps
  - token_cost_hour = 1.95 / (4560 * 3600) ≈ 1.19e-7 $/token => cost_per_1k_tokens ≈ $0.000119

Interpreting the numbers (working heuristics):
- Use accuracy_delta_pct vs quality_budget_pct to triage: if accuracy_delta_pct <= quality_budget_pct then config is candidate.
- Otherwise compute quality-normalized cost: normalized_cost = cost_per_1k_tokens * (1 + max(0, accuracy_delta_pct - quality_budget_pct)/5)
  - rationale: percent drops above budget are penalized; divisor tuned as subjective sensitivity parameter.
- Recommendation rules (simple):
  - keep: accuracy_delta_pct <= 0.5 * quality_budget_pct and relative_cost_vs_fp16 < 0.8
  - consider: accuracy_delta_pct <= quality_budget_pct and relative_cost_vs_fp16 between 0.6 and 1.2
  - avoid: accuracy_delta_pct > quality_budget_pct or relative_cost_vs_fp16 > 1.4

Batching and latency caveats (notes to product):
- microbench peak_tokens_per_sec often measured under ideal conditions; production tail latency and cold-starts can change effective throughput.
- For interactive low-latency apps, use conservative batch_size (e.g., 1-8) and measure p95 latency separately.
- For high throughput APIs, prefer the cost-per-token model above but validate with a 24hr traffic replay.

Scan algorithm (copyable checklist for engineers):
1) Populate baseline FP16 row (measured microbench numbers + chosen reference GPU cost).
2) Fill candidate quant rows with microbench numbers from small-sample runs (3-5 runs, avg tps).
3) Set product quality_budget_pct (from PM).
4) Compute cost_per_1k_tokens & relative_cost_vs_fp16.
5) Flag configs where accuracy_delta_pct <= quality_budget_pct.
6) Rank flagged configs by cost_per_1k_tokens ascending and present top-2 as candidates for canary testing.
7) Add p95 latency measurement for canary and recompute effective user-facing cost (if latency SLOs cause capacity overprovisioning, adjust).

Suggested follow-ups / experiments to validate sampler:
- Run 1-hour throughput replay for top-2 candidates on dedicated pool and compare measured p95 and cost.
- Add a small evaluation harness that computes exact eval metric on a held-out prompt set and stores metric + delta in a dashboard.
- Integrate with `optimize` product scoring: allow product to pass quality_budget_pct and weight latency vs cost preferences.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tune the penalty divisor in normalized_cost formula (currently 5). Needs A/B with real traffic.
- Decide canonical reference GPU list and map gpu_hour_cost values to our pricing tiers.
- Add support for mixed-precision and layerwise quant knobs (e.g., outlier-aware 4bit for attention).

Scratch area (short quick formulas and cheat sheet):
- rough_tokens_per_sec ~ O(memory_bandwidth * kernel_efficiency / seq_length) (qualitative)
- expected_speedup_int8_vs_fp16 ~= 1.2-1.6 (depends on kernel & hw)
- expected_speedup_4bit_vs_fp16 ~= 1.6-2.4 on quant-friendly kernels

Notes: keep this sheet in the product/optimize folder as a lightweight triage tool. When we pick winners, move canonical numbers into the quant-econ-playground worksheet and link to rollout runbooks.

Recent edits: 2024-12-05: updated example numbers to reflect new p4d pricing; removed an earlier 'latency_penalty' column pending better measurement.

Questions for reviewer (PM/ML eng):
- Is the 2% quality_budget reasonable for downstream ranking tasks? (PM input required)
- Do we prefer an absolute accuracy delta or relative metric like MRR drop?

End of sheet.
